reviewer: escalate: a drop-rule function over --name-status diff records alone cannot tell a partial multi-file deletion (sibling file untouched) from a full case drop, so the design as specced is unimplementable
advocate: continue: add a survivor-path argument to the drop rule, sourced through the existing committed-ref idiom already in scope, plus one missing acceptance test, rather than park on a testability sentence
decision: Continue phase (b): spec.md Design's drop-rule bullet now says the function also takes a survivor-path list for the eval-case rule, read via a new plugin/gate/diff.py helper tree_files(root, ref, prefix) built on git ls-tree -r --name-only <ref> -- <prefix> (argument-list, no shell=True) called at ctx.diff.head; plan.md's Proof list gains test_ratchets_eval_case_partial_delete_is_not_a_drop.
rationale: Both verdicts agree on the fact: a records-only pure function cannot distinguish a partial multi-file eval-case deletion from a full drop, since an untouched sibling file leaves no diff record at all.

They disagree only on remedy: the advocate's fix is concrete and scoped to a file plan.md already lists (diff.py), reuses the codebase's existing committed-ref pattern (ctx.diff.head, the same ref file_at/_cat_ok already read), and adds no shell string or new scope.

Half the reviewer's stated harm is wrong: a three-dot diff already lists every D across multiple commits, so 'under-detect drops spread across commits' cannot occur; this weakens the case for a full park.

Safer reading favors applying the fix now: a park returns the whole change to design over a sentence this commit can correct, while continuing with the design edit above closes the real gap and adds the missing test the advocate names.
Nothing here touches a guardrail file, a limit, or a risk-list item; the drop-rule signature and the one test are the only changes, both inside spec.md/plan.md which this phase owns.
